title: 示例题组：Rooftop Farms（1 篇 10 题）

passage.title: Why Cities Are Turning to Rooftop Farms
paras: On a summer morning in Singapore, office workers taking the lift to the twentieth floor of a commercial tower may be surprised to find rows of lettuce and basil growing where air-conditioning units once stood. Rooftop farming, once dismissed as a hobby for idealists, has quietly become part of how some crowded cities think about food.

The appeal is partly practical. Land at street level is expensive, but roofs are largely unused. A farm on top of a building also shortens the journey from soil to plate: vegetables harvested in the morning can reach a restaurant downstairs by lunchtime, losing little of their freshness. Supporters add that plants absorb heat, which can lower the temperature of the floors beneath them and reduce the energy needed for cooling.

Yet the numbers do not always add up. Strengthening an old roof to carry the weight of wet soil can cost more than the farm will earn in a decade. Water must be pumped upward, and strong winds limit which crops can survive. For these reasons, most rooftop farms grow light, fast-growing greens rather than staple crops such as rice or potatoes.

Critics therefore argue that rooftop farms will never feed a city. Their defenders do not entirely disagree. What the farms offer, they say, is not self-sufficiency but connection: children who have never seen a vegetable growing can watch one appear over a few weeks, and residents who meet among the planting beds begin to treat their building as a neighbourhood. Measured only in tonnes of food, the farms are small. Measured in what they teach people about where food comes from, they may be considerably larger.

items.q: The word "dismissed" in Paragraph 1 is closest in meaning to ____.
According to Paragraph 2, vegetables reach the restaurant "losing little of their freshness" because they ____.
What can be inferred about the floors directly below a rooftop farm?
o: They are usually used as restaurants.
They may need less energy for cooling.
They are more expensive to rent.

items.q: "The numbers do not always add up" (Paragraph 3) suggests that rooftop farming ____.
o: has been exaggerated by the media

items.q: Why do most rooftop farms grow light greens?
o: Weight, water and wind limit the choice.
Staple crops are cheap to buy.

items.q: In "Strengthening an old roof to carry the weight of wet soil can cost more than…", what is the subject of "can cost"?
"Their defenders do not entirely disagree" means the defenders ____.
o: accept that the farms cannot feed a city

items.q: According to the defenders, the main value of rooftop farms lies in ____.
How is the passage mainly organized?
o: A problem followed by one solution
Benefits, limits, then a new view of value

items.q: The author's attitude toward rooftop farms is best described as ____.
o: balanced, seeing value beyond food output
